rules.statement: Serve an OpenAPI document and its reference UI page only when a host configuration switch turns each one on, with both switches off by default in every environment and no environment checks inside the library.
rules.why: Publishing an API description is the operator's choice, and a deployment that doesn't want it must get neither the document nor the page from the defaults. Environment decisions belong in one place, not in library defaults.
rules.check: Look for MapOpenApi/MapScalarApiReference (or a wrapper around them) that is mapped unconditionally, options that default to true, or IHostEnvironment.IsDevelopment() checks inside a library's mapping extension.

rules.statement: When one option needs another (for example, a reference page that renders a document needs the document enabled), enforce it with an options validator that fails when the host starts.
rules.why: The page renders the document, so enabling the page without the document is a misconfiguration that should fail at startup rather than at request time.
rules.check: Look for new dependent option flags that have no IValidateOptions validator, or no ValidateOnStart, to reject an invalid combination.

rules.statement: Pre-fill client credentials or any secret into a served OpenAPI document or API reference UI configuration only in Development. Elsewhere, leave the operator to type them into the Authorize dialog.
rules.why: A pre-filled secret is baked into served configuration where anyone who reaches the page can read it, which breaks the rule that no secret material appears on the public surface.
rules.check: Look for client ids, secrets, or tokens that come from configuration and are passed to Scalar or Swagger authentication pre-fill, or to OpenAPI examples, without a Development-only guard.

rules.statement: Configure an API reference UI page to load nothing from a third party: disable the renderer's telemetry, AI agent, MCP integration and CDN fonts, and keep authentication state in memory rather than enabling persistent authentication.
rules.why: The renderer's defaults reach third-party services from the visitor's browser, and persisted authentication keeps credentials beyond the session.
rules.check: Look at the Scalar (or other renderer) options for telemetry, agent, MCP, or CDN font settings left at their defaults, and for EnablePersistentAuthentication.

rules.statement: Serve a server-rendered API reference page under the strict Content-Security-Policy, using a fresh nonce per response that is passed to the renderer's scripts and exposed to its stylesheet, plus connect-src 'self', frame-ancestors 'none' and no-store.
rules.why: The reference page is a page the server writes, so it falls under the strict CSP that applies to every such page.
rules.check: Look for a reference UI endpoint that skips the shared HTML page security helper, reuses a nonce across responses, or loosens script-src, style-src, or connect-src.

rules.statement: Don't report an enabled OpenAPI document being served anonymously as an exposure that needs a token gate.
rules.why: The document is the same for every deployment of a version and derives from open-source code, so a gate hides nothing. The reference page's browser fetch carries no token, so a gate would break it. Turning the document off is the control.
rules.check: Before reporting, confirm the document is served behind an off-by-default configuration switch. If it is, don't ask for authorization on the document endpoint.

rules.statement: Shape form-urlencoded request bodies in the OpenAPI document itself: mark each field that must be pre-filled `required` and give its schema a `Default`, and don't rely on a renderer applying a named example.
rules.why: Renderers leave optional form properties unchecked and leave them out of the request, and they don't apply named examples to form fields.
rules.check: Look for document transformers that add a named example for an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body when they should set required and a schema default.

rules.statement: Give every error status an endpoint declares a description that says when that status occurs, never a bare reason phrase such as "Conflict" or "Not Found".
rules.why: A client author reads the description to decide how to handle the answer, and a bare reason phrase only says that the route can fail, not when.
rules.check: Look for declared Produces/ProducesProblem statuses whose XML `<response>` is missing or only restates the HTTP reason phrase.

rules.statement: In a minimal API handler's XML documentation, use `<response code="N">` only for the route's own reasons (what it validates, which resource a 404 names, its own conflicts). Write status meanings shared by a route group once, in a group-level operation transformer, and don't repeat them on each route.
rules.why: A shared sentence written on every route repeats and drifts, so a change to one shared meaning would miss routes.
rules.check: Look for `<response>` text on a handler that duplicates a shared meaning (missing token, lacking authority, If-Match mismatch, non-JSON body, service unavailable) already supplied by the group transformer.

rules.statement: Give each status code at most one `<response>` element in a handler method's XML documentation.
rules.why: The Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi source generator reads only one `<response>` per status code.
rules.check: Look for a status code that appears in two `<response code>` elements on the same method.

rules.statement: Put minimal API response descriptions in the handler's XML `<response>` documentation, not in endpoint metadata such as IProducesResponseTypeMetadata.
rules.why: ApiExplorer drops a description set on a minimal API's response metadata, so it never reaches the OpenAPI document.
rules.check: Look for custom metadata or Produces calls that try to carry a response description string.

rules.statement: Make each project that maps documented API routes reference Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi and call AddOpenApi, so the source generator carries its handlers' XML documentation into the document.
rules.why: The generator runs only in projects that reference the package and call AddOpenApi. Without it, the handlers' descriptions never reach the document.
rules.check: Look for a new package or project that maps API endpoints with `<response>` docs but doesn't reference Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi or call AddOpenApi.

rules.statement: Register OpenAPI document contributions that describe a library's endpoints (tags, security schemes, examples) in the library's own registration, not in each host's Program.cs.
rules.why: The document describes the server's own endpoints, and hosts that re-declare its contributions drift from one another.
rules.check: Look for hosts adding document transformers, security schemes, or tag groups for endpoints that a library owns.

rules.statement: In a test project, include a test asserting that every status each API route declares has a description in the handler's XML docs or in the shared set, and that no error response in the generated document keeps its bare reason phrase.
rules.why: Tests pin the descriptions, so a route that declares a status its handler doesn't describe fails until its XML documentation explains it.
rules.check: When a diff adds routes or declared statuses, check that they are covered by the description theory or document test, and that those tests aren't weakened.
